data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Selective Chopper Radiometer (SCR)
record.description: The Nimbus 5 Selective Chopper Radiometer (SCR) was designed to (1) observe the global temperature structure of the atmosphere up to 50 km in altitude, (2) make supporting observations of water vapor distribution, and (3) determine the density of ice particles in cirrus clouds. To accomplish these objectives, the SCR measured emitted radiation in 16 spectral intervals separated into the following four groups: (1) four CO2 channels between 13.8 and 14.8 micrometers, (2) four channels at 15.0 micrometers, (3) an IR window channel at 11.1 micrometers, a water vapor channel at 18.6 micrometers, two channels at 49.5 and 133.3 micrometers, and (4) four channels at 2.08, 2.59, 2.65,and 3.5 micrometers. From an average satellite altitude of 1100 km, the radiometer viewed a 48-km circle on the earth's surface with a ground resolution of about 25 km. A similar experiment was flown on Nimbus 4. For a more detailed description, see Section 6 in "The Nimbus 5 User's Guide" (TRF B14758), available from NSSDC. Both NSSDC and SDSD have data.
